# Sprig — Design & Brand Guidelines

**Sprig** is an unofficial, native-feeling WhatsApp Web client for Ubuntu / Linux desktops.

**Version:** 1.0.0

> ⚠️ **Not affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta.** "WhatsApp" is a trademark of Meta Platforms, Inc.
> Sprig is a third-party wrapper around WhatsApp Web. The app name, icon, and colors are
> deliberately distinct from WhatsApp's official branding (see *Trademark & Colour Safety* below).

---

## Overview

§9 · Overview *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

Sprig is a desktop client for WhatsApp Web on Ubuntu and other Linux desktops: one window, the
chats you already have, notifications and a tray icon that behave like a native app. **The
audience** is Linux users who keep WhatsApp open all day and are tired of a browser tab.
**The personality** is a well-behaved GNOME citizen — it follows the system's light/dark
preference, its fonts and its spacing, and adds only a green leaf of its own. **It is not**
WhatsApp, not affiliated with Meta, and never looks as if it were (§2).

---

## 1. Name

**Primary: `Sprig`**

Why it works:
- A *sprig* is a small green shoot — it justifies a green palette on its own botanical terms
  rather than as an imitation of WhatsApp, which keeps you clear of trademark trouble.
- Short (one syllable), easy to type as a package name (`sprig`), and available-feeling.
- The leaf motif gives the icon a distinctive mark instead of copying WhatsApp's phone-in-bubble.

Tagline: **"A native WhatsApp client for Linux."** (use "for WhatsApp Web" in store copy,
never brand *as* WhatsApp).

**Name — confirmed 2026-09-26 (D-081).** Checked that day: no `sprig` package on the AUR,
no `sprig` snap on Snapcraft, and the Flathub app-id `com.adommo.sprig` is unused. The
name stands; the alternatives below are kept as the record and are **not** in use.

**Alternatives** (recorded, not adopted):
| Name | Angle |
|------|-------|
| Verda | "green" (Italian/Esperanto), soft and modern |
| Chatterleaf | explicit chat + leaf, more descriptive |
| Wisp | a wisp of conversation; airy, minimal |
| Fernly | fern → green, friendly consumer feel |

**App-id — decided: `com.adommo.sprig`.** Flathub requires the app-id to be the reverse of
a domain the publisher controls, and `adommo.com` is. *(Was: "check availability … e.g.
`com.adommo.sprig`"; `com.example` is a placeholder and can never
ship.)*

---

## 2. Trademark & Colour Safety

The brief was: *similar to WhatsApp, but not the same.* Here's how Sprig threads that:

- **Same family, measurably different shade.** WhatsApp's signature green is `#25D366`
  (a yellow-leaning green). Sprig's primary is `#16B364` → rendered here as a
  `#2AC66C → #12915A` gradient — a slightly more **emerald** green. Recognizable as
  "the green messaging app family," but a distinct hex, hue, and lightness.
- **Different mark.** WhatsApp uses a telephone handset inside a speech bubble. Sprig uses a
  **leaf** inside a speech bubble. The speech-bubble shape is generic; the interior symbol is not.
- **No official assets.** Never ship WhatsApp's real logo, wordmark, or exact green. Never imply
  endorsement. Keep the disclaimer visible in the About dialog and store listing.

| Role | WhatsApp (avoid copying) | Sprig (use) |
|------|--------------------------|-------------|
| Signature green | `#25D366` | `#16B364` |
| Deep teal | `#075E54` | `#0C6B4E` |
| Light bubble tint | `#DCF8C6` | `#E7F6EC` |

## 4. Logo

**Concept:** a leaf resting inside a rounded speech bubble on a green squircle — "conversation
that grows." The leaf's midrib and veins double as a subtle chat/growth cue.

**Icon-only colours.** The app icon uses two gradients and a soft shadow that are not part
of the UI palette and must not be used in the interface:

| element | value |
|---|---|
| squircle ground | `#2AC66C` → `#12915A` (vertical) |
| leaf | `#1FB365` → `#0E8A54` (diagonal) |
| shadow | `#053A25` @ 18% |

> **Documented (approved).** These three values appear in the app icon but were recorded
> nowhere. Anything an asset needs belongs in this document.

**Files (shipped):**
- `assets/svg/icon.svg` — full-colour app icon (master, scalable)
- `assets/hicolor/{512,256,128,64}.png` — rasterised for the hicolor icon theme

**Files (shipped 2026-09-02):**
- `assets/svg/logo-wordmark-{light,dark}.svg` — the wordmark alone, outlined
- `assets/svg/logo-{light,dark}.svg` — horizontal lockup: mark height 1.30× the wordmark ink
  height, gap 0.42× mark width, vertically centred

> The icon keeps its own gradients inside the lockup. Per the icon-only colour rule above, those
> gradients must still never appear in the interface.

**Files (shipped 2026-08-29):**
- `assets/svg/sprig-symbolic.svg` — monochrome mark for tray/status icons (`currentColor`)
  > **Built 2026-08-29.** This file was previously listed as shipped but did not exist. §7 (tray)
  > and the minimum-size rule both depend on it, so it was created in Phase 4 as
  > `assets/svg/sprig-symbolic.svg`.

**Construction / clear space:** the icon sits on a 512-unit grid with a `112` corner radius.
Keep clear space around the mark equal to the corner radius when placing on other surfaces.

**Minimum sizes:** color icon down to 32 px; below that, use `sprig-symbolic.svg`.

### Do
- Use the master SVG and export fresh rasters per size.
- Recolor the symbolic version via `currentColor` for light/dark trays.

### Don't
- Don't recolor the mark into WhatsApp's exact `#25D366`.
- Don't add WhatsApp's handset glyph or wordmark.
- Don't stretch, rotate, or add drop shadows beyond the built-in one.

## Typography

§5

**App UI — system faces, nothing bundled.** Use fonts that ship on Ubuntu so there's no
bundling overhead:

| Role | Font | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| UI / body | **Ubuntu**, falling back to `system-ui` | **14px** base |
| Monospace (code blocks, IDs) | **Ubuntu Mono**, falling back to `monospace` | 13px |

*Pinned 2026-09-26 (D-081). Was "Ubuntu (or system Inter), 14–15 px" and "Ubuntu Mono /
JetBrains Mono". Inter and JetBrains Mono are dropped: nothing is bundled, so a named
alternative only helps if it happens to be installed, and JetBrains Mono is Adommo's mono.*

**Type scale (desktop, px):** 12 timestamps and metadata · 13 mono · **14 body and message
text** · 15 chat names (500) · 16 conversation header (700) · 20 dialog titles (700) · 24
empty-state heading (700).

**Wordmark — Rubik 500, outlined to paths.** *(added 2026-09-02)*

The rule above is about the **running application**, and it is unchanged: nothing is bundled into
the app. It never covered the *wordmark*, and this was the only brand in the portfolio where the
name is never set as type — there was an icon and a symbolic mark, and no logotype at all.

| | |
|---|---|
| Face | **Rubik** 500, SIL OFL 1.1 |
| Tracking | −0.01em |
| Delivery | **outlined to vector paths** — no runtime font dependency |
| Vendored | `assets/fonts/`, as a **build input only** |

**Why not Ubuntu.** It is the face §5 already names, and it was the obvious choice — but Ubuntu
carries **Canonical's** identity. A third-party client that works this hard to stay visually
distinct from WhatsApp (§2) should not borrow another organisation's brand face for its own
logotype. Rubik's rounded terminals echo the squircle and the leaf, and no other brand in the
portfolio uses it.

**Cantarell was considered and rejected:** it is GNOME's UI face, which fits the desktop context,
but Google Fonts publishes only 400 and 700 — no 500, the weight this wordmark needs.

Weights: 400 body, 500 for names/emphasis, 700 for headers. Line height **1.45** for message text, 1.3 for names and headers.

---

## Layout

§6

Two-pane WhatsApp-Web-style shell:
- **Left rail (chats):** **360px** default, resizable 280–480px, search on top, list below,
  unread badges in Sprig Green.
- **Right pane (conversation):** header (avatar + name + status), scrollback, composer.
- **Density:** 12px gutters, 8px inter-bubble spacing (2px within one sender's run), bubbles
  max-width **70%** of pane.
- Honor the GNOME/Ubuntu **libadwaita** light/dark preference; don't force a theme.

*Values pinned 2026-09-26 (D-081); were "~360 px" and "~70%".*

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Spacing grid | 4px — scale 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 |
| Window minimum | 720 × 480; below 800px wide the rail collapses and the conversation takes the window, with a back button (libadwaita adaptive) |
| Chat row | 64px (avatar 44px) |
| Header bar | 48px, libadwaita `HeaderBar` |
| Composer | 56px min, grows to 6 lines |
| Touch/click target min | 32px (desktop pointer), 44px on touch-enabled devices |

**Motion:** follow libadwaita — 200ms `ease-out` for pane transitions, none elsewhere. Honour
the GNOME "Reduce animation" setting.

---

## Elevation & Depth

§10 · Elevation *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

Follow libadwaita: the window is flat; only transient surfaces lift.

| Level | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| base — window, rail, conversation | `background` / `surface` | `background` / `surface` |
| bubble | incoming `surface-sunken`, outgoing `#D9F2E1` — no border, no shadow | incoming `#1E2A24`, outgoing `#124A38` |
| popover, menu | `surface` + libadwaita popover shadow | `surface` + 1px `border` |
| dialog | `surface` + libadwaita dialog shadow over a `rgba(0,0,0,0.30)` dim | same, dim `rgba(0,0,0,0.50)` |

The app icon's soft shadow (§4) is icon-only and never appears in the UI.

---

## Shapes

§11 · Shape *(added 2026-09-26, D-081 — was front-matter `omitted: rounded`)*

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Corner radius | **6px** buttons, inputs · **12px** bubbles, cards, dialogs, popovers · **4px** the bubble corner nearest the sender's side on the last bubble of a run · 999px unread badge and avatar |
| Border width | 1px divider · 2px focus ring (libadwaita accent) |

These match libadwaita's own radii, so Sprig's widgets sit next to system widgets without a
seam. The app icon's squircle (`112` on 512) is icon-only.

---

## Components

§12 · Component library specification *(added 2026-09-26, D-081)*

Build on libadwaita widgets; restyle only colour. Every component in light and dark.

- **Chat row** — avatar 44px, name (15/500), last message (14, `text-muted`, one line),
  timestamp (12), unread badge (`accent` fill, **ink** count — never white, §3), muted icon,
  pinned icon; selected = `surface-sunken`.
- **Conversation header** — avatar, name, status ("online", "typing…", last seen), search and
  overflow buttons.
- **Message bubble** — incoming / outgoing; text, image, video, voice note, document, reply
  quote, forwarded label, reaction row; timestamp and ticks inside the bubble bottom-right
  (ticks `#0C6B4E` light / `#2AC66C` dark).
- **Composer** — emoji, attach, text field (grows to 6 lines), voice-record/send button
  (`accent` fill, ink icon).
- **Attachment popover** — photo/video, document, camera, contact.
- **Search** — in rail (chats) and in conversation (messages), with match highlight.
- **Login screen** — WhatsApp Web's QR code centred, one line of instruction, the
  not-affiliated disclaimer below it.
- **Connection banner** — "Phone not connected" / "Reconnecting…" — `surface-sunken`, icon +
  text, not a colour alone.
- **Notification** — desktop portal; sender and first line; respects "hide message content".
- **Tray menu** — Show Sprig · Do not disturb · Quit, on `sprig-symbolic.svg`.
- **Preferences dialog** — libadwaita `PreferencesWindow`: Appearance (follow system / light /
  dark), Notifications, Start on login, Close to tray, Spell check.
- **About dialog** — libadwaita `AboutWindow` with the disclaimer (§2) in the description.
- **States** — empty rail ("No chats yet"), no conversation selected (leaf mark + "Choose a
  chat"), offline, error.
- **Iconography** — the system's Adwaita symbolic icons, `currentColor`, 16px; no bundled icon
  set, consistent with nothing-bundled (§5).

## Do's and Don'ts

§13 · Do / Don't *(added 2026-09-26, D-081 — consolidates §2, §3, §4, §8)*

| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
|---|---|
| Use Sprig Green `#16B364` as a fill with ink on it | Put white text on Sprig Green (2.74:1) |
| Use Fern `#0C6B4E` / `#2AC66C` for accent text and links | Use Sprig Green as a text colour |
| Follow the system light/dark preference and fonts | Force a theme or bundle a UI font |
| Say "Sprig" and "for WhatsApp Web" | Call the app WhatsApp or imply Meta's endorsement |
| Keep the disclaimer in About, login and store listings | Ship WhatsApp's logo, handset glyph, wordmark or `#25D366` |
| Keep gradients and the soft shadow inside the app icon | Use the icon's gradients or shadow in the UI |
| Use `sprig-symbolic.svg` below 32px and in the tray | Scale the colour icon below 32px |

## 6.5 Asset manifest — desktop-app variant

Sprig is a Linux desktop client, not a web property, so the repo's standard
`ASSET_MANIFEST.md` does not apply unchanged. This brand's required set is:

**Applies:**
| asset | status |
|---|---|
| `assets/svg/icon.svg` — scalable master | present |
| `assets/hicolor/{64,128,256,512}.png` — hicolor theme sizes | present |
| `assets/svg/sprig-symbolic.svg` — monochrome `currentColor` tray/status mark | present (built 2026-08-29) |
| `.desktop` entry | belongs to the app repo, not this one |

**Does not apply** (no web surface): `og-image.png`, `site.webmanifest`,
`apple-touch-icon.png`, `favicon.ico`, `favicon.svg`, maskable PWA icons.

**No marketing page — decided 2026-09-26 (D-081).** *Was: "if a marketing or download page is
added later … revisit".* The Flathub and Snap Store listings and the repository README are the
storefront. A Linux desktop client is discovered in the software centre, not on the web, and a
page would add a web asset set to maintain for no install path it does not already have.

---

## 7. Ubuntu Integration Notes

- **Packaging — decided 2026-09-26 (D-081):** **Flatpak on Flathub is primary**; **Snap** is
  also published because Ubuntu's App Center lists snaps first; a **`.deb`** ships on GitHub
  Releases for direct installs. No AUR package is maintained by us. Include a `.desktop` file
  and the app-id `com.adommo.sprig`. *(Was "Flatpak and/or Snap".)*
- **Icons:** install PNGs into `hicolor/{64,128,256,512}x{...}/apps/` and the SVG into
  `hicolor/scalable/apps/`; the symbolic goes in `.../symbolic/apps/`.
- **Notifications:** use the desktop portal / libnotify; badge unread count on the icon where
  the shell supports it.
- **Tray:** use `sprig-symbolic.svg` so it adapts to light/dark panels.
- **Implementation — decided 2026-09-26 (D-081): Electron.** *(Was "Electron or Tauri".)*
  Tauri on Linux renders with WebKitGTK, and WhatsApp Web's calls, voice notes and media are
  built and tested against Chromium; a lighter wrapper that breaks on a WhatsApp deploy costs
  more than the ~100MB it saves. Keep the wrapper thin, respect WhatsApp Web's TOS, and store
  nothing beyond local session state.

---

## 8. Voice

Friendly, plain, unbranded. Refer to the app as "Sprig," never as "WhatsApp." In first-run and
About screens, state clearly that Sprig is an independent client and link to the disclaimer.

## Colour ramps — derived 2026-09-02

This document defined only the **semantic roles** (background, text, accent, border…).
The intermediate steps those roles are drawn from were never written down, so
`tokens.json` and `theme.css` had no ramps while seventeen other brands did.

**These are derived, not invented from taste.** Each ramp is interpolated in CIELAB
between values this brand **already ships**, and those values are pinned as exact
anchors — no colour already in use has moved:

| anchor | is | and equals |
|---|---|---|
| `slate-50` | the lightest neutral | the light-mode `background` |
| `slate-950` | the darkest neutral | the light-mode `text` |
| `leaf-400` | the accent at its lightest usable step | the **dark-mode** `accent` |
| `leaf-700` | the accent at its darkest | the **light-mode** `accent` |

`leaf-300` extrapolates one step lighter than 400 by the same per-step delta, so it is a
real step rather than a duplicate of its neighbour.

**A ramp step is not a role.** These are fixed colours, identical in both modes. Use the
semantic token wherever one exists; reach for a raw step only where no role covers it.

### Neutral — slate

| Token | Hex |
|---|---|
| slate-50 | `#F7FBF8` |
| slate-100 | `#DDE2DF` |
| slate-200 | `#C3CAC6` |
| slate-300 | `#AAB2AD` |

| slate-700 | `#4D5A54` |
